unit.why: A single memorate, passed down through a chain of tellers, about the Kozhnitzer Maggid receiving a night visit from the departed R. Ber of Mezritch, as seen by his young grandson.

stories.start_quote: במכתב מחו׳ הגאבד״ק פלונסק וז"ל שמעתי
stories.end_quote: גילוי צדיקים איז גרעסיר וויא גילוי אליהו
stories.summary_en: As a six- or seven-year-old sleeping beside his grandfather the Maggid, the future rebbe of Mogielnica saw a visitor at night who walked with the Maggid without the usual deference; he took him for Elijah, but the Maggid told him it was R. Ber (of Mezritch) and that the revelation of tzaddikim is greater than the revelation of Elijah.

quotes: ישן במטה אחת את זקינו המגיד זי"ע
tags.why: The witness is the Maggid's grandson, sleeping in his bed.

quotes: והמגיד הלך אתו על פני חדרו רצוא ושוב
tags.why: The Maggid meets and walks with the soul of his late master.

quotes: גילוי צדיקים איז גרעסיר וויא גילוי אליהו
tags.why: A departed tzaddik is revealed, and the story names this a 'giluy'.

quotes: כי ראה כי האיש לא דיבר עם המגיד
tags.why: The child sees the supernatural visitor while awake.

quotes: וחשב בלבו שבטח זהו אליהו הנביא
tags.why: The visitor's true identity is disclosed only afterwards.

quotes: וחשב בלבו שבטח זהו אליהו הנביא
tags.why: Elijah is supposed by the child and used as the comparison, though he does not actually appear.

quotes: ששמע בעצמו מפי מחו' הרה״ק ממאגלינצא שסיפר לפני הרב החסיד
tags.why: The tale is framed as told by the Mogielnica rebbe before R. Hirshele of Tomaszów.
The Maggid's late master visits him after death.
